audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a single Nautilus ability — it says "Q hook", "passive auto-root", "point-blank E and R knockup". Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide and Depth Charge appear nowhere.
audit.why: This is the packet's flagged defect and it is real. Titan's Wrath and Riptide are not merely unnamed, they are absent as mechanics: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that makes his autos deal damage over time to you and everything around you, and Riptide is a 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s triple slow. Those two are what actually win his extended trades, and a Nasus reading this has no idea either exists.
audit.corrected: Name all five and add the two missing mechanics.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late calls him "an immobile single-target tank" who "cannot escape your empowered Q", and content.mid says he is "immobile apart from that hook".
audit.why: Dredge Line colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus to the terrain. In a side lane, which is exactly the scenario content.late is describing, that is a real escape over any wall — the lane is lined with them. A Nasus who commits Ghost and a stacked Q believing his target physically cannot leave will lose the kill and the tempo.
audit.corrected: He is not immobile: Dredge Line into a wall yanks him to it. Cut him off from terrain before you commit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nautilus.json (Q: 'Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it')

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns lists Dredge Line twice as two different entries, carries no numbers, and calls it "His only engage".
audit.why: It is duplicated boilerplate. Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — a 14-second punish window at rank 1, the most actionable number in a lane whose entire win condition is "dodge the hook", and it outranges Wither's 700 so he engages from outside your answer. Depth Charge is a second engage tool on 120/100/80s, so "his only engage" is wrong.
audit.corrected: Give Dredge Line its real cooldown and range, note the 1150-vs-700 gap, and list Depth Charge as the second engage.

audit.why: 52.66% over 1595 games, the largest sample in my slice, and the EVEN / 6/10 label plus the level chart (Nautilus level 1, skill 2-3, Nasus from 4 on) match it.

edits.before: Nautilus is one of the few melee tanks who can actually punish your weak early — his Q hook plus the passive root on his first auto can chain enough CC to set up a gank before you have Wither to break it. Don't last-hit from behind your caster minions or step into hook range over open ground; soak Q farm at max range and accept you concede levels 1-2. The good news is his poke is nonexistent and once you respect the hook there's nothing here he can do to you alone.
edits.after: Nautilus is one of the few melee tanks who can actually punish your weak early — Dredge Line (Q) plus Staggering Blow, the root on his first auto against you, chains enough CC to set up a gank before you have Wither. Don't last-hit from behind your caster minions or step into hook range over open ground; soak Q farm at max range and accept you concede levels 1-2. Dredge Line is a 14s cooldown at rank 1, so once it misses that whole window is yours.

edits.before: At 3 Wither flips everything — point-and-click his attack speed and movement to a crawl the instant he hooks, and his all-in falls apart because he's immobile apart from that hook. By 6 your Fury of the Sands plus Wither wins any committed fight: he walks up to you, you slow him to nothing, Spirit Fire shreds his armor, and your lifesteal eats his trade damage. Bait the hook, sidestep or eat it with Wither ready, then run him down.
edits.after: At 3 Wither flips everything — point-and-click his attack speed and movement to a crawl the instant Dredge Line lands. Titan's Wrath (W) is his real trade tool, a flat 12s shield that makes his autos burn you and the wave, and Riptide (E) slows you again every 5-7s, so never chase without Wither up. By 6 Fury of the Sands plus Wither wins any committed fight: Spirit Fire shreds his armor and your lifesteal eats his trade damage.

edits.before: This is exactly the matchup you scale into — an immobile single-target tank with no percent-HP or true damage, which is everything your stacked Q and fat HP bar feast on. In a sidelane he cannot 1v1 you, cannot escape your empowered Q, and his hook+knockup just feeds him into Wither. Your only real loss condition is his teamfight pick potential, so push the side and force him to answer your splitpush alone, where he simply can't.
edits.after: This is exactly the matchup you scale into — a single-target tank with no percent-HP or true damage, which is everything your stacked Q and fat HP bar feast on. In a sidelane he cannot 1v1 you and Depth Charge just feeds him into Wither. He is not immobile though: Dredge Line into a wall yanks him over it, so cut him off from terrain before you commit or he walks away. His pick potential is your real loss condition.

edits.before: Nautilus's Q hook into passive auto-root is his cleanest kill window before you have Wither — hug the wave and never stand behind your caster minions.
edits.after: Dredge Line into Staggering Blow's auto-root is his cleanest kill window before Wither — hug the wave and never stand behind your caster minions.

edits.before: Reach Wither at 3 so his hook+root combo can't lock you for a full all-in
edits.after: Reach Wither at 3 so Dredge Line into Staggering Blow can't lock a full all-in

edits.before: Use his point-blank E and R knockup to set up jungle ganks while you're immobile
edits.after: Use Riptide (E) and Depth Charge (R) to set up jungle ganks while you're immobile

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Nautilus Dredge Line: Hurls an anchor; on a champ hit, pulls both together — his hook. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Q): matchup-defining — 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range, so it outranges Wither. Dodge it. - Nautilus Depth Charge (R): 120/100/80s knockup that finds you anywhere inside 825 — his second engage.

notes: Left alone deliberately: both layers tell the player never to stand behind their caster minions against the hook. Whether that is right turns on Dredge Line's minion-collision behaviour — if it stops on a minion the wave protects you, but if it stops on a minion and pulls Nautilus to it, standing there feeds him a free gap-close. Riot's text says only 'Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together', and the kit's needsResearch.minionBlock is empty, which means unknown rather than no. I could not settle it from local data so I reproduced the sentence verbatim inside my rewrites rather than reverse it. Worth a League Wiki check before anyone edits it. The packet's suspectName 'Spirit Fire's' in whys[3] is a false positive — that is Nasus's own E, correctly named.
